topics.label: Single-Page Apps
topics.desc: Architecture where the browser loads one HTML shell and JavaScript swaps views client-side, powering app-like UIs in React, Vue, and Angular.

topics.label: Component Model
topics.desc: Encapsulated, composable UI units with props, children, and slots that form the building blocks of React, Vue, Svelte, and every modern framework.

topics.label: Declarative UI
topics.desc: Describing UI as a pure function of state so the framework reconciles the DOM for you, the core idea behind React and SwiftUI-style frameworks.

topics.label: Virtual DOM & Reconciliation
topics.desc: In-memory element tree diffed against the previous render to compute minimal DOM mutations, the update strategy used by React and Vue.

topics.label: Reactivity & Signals
topics.desc: Fine-grained dependency tracking that re-runs only affected computations, the model behind Solid signals, Vue refs, Svelte runes, and Angular signals.

topics.label: One-Way Data Flow
topics.desc: State flows down via props and changes flow up via events or callbacks, making updates predictable across React and Flux-style architectures.

topics.label: SPA Tradeoffs
topics.desc: Weighing rich interactivity against large bundles, SEO gaps, and slow first paint, the tension that motivated SSR meta-frameworks like Next.js.

topics.label: React
topics.desc: Meta's declarative library for building component-based UIs with a virtual DOM and hooks, the dominant frontend framework and de facto industry standard.

topics.label: JSX
topics.desc: HTML-like syntax compiled to createElement calls that lets React components describe markup inline in JavaScript, transpiled by Babel or SWC.

topics.label: Components & Props
topics.desc: Functions that take read-only props and return JSX, the unit of reuse in React, composed via children and stable keys for list rendering.

topics.label: useState
topics.desc: The core React hook that adds local reactive state to a function component and triggers a re-render whenever its setter is called.

topics.label: useEffect
topics.desc: React hook for running side effects like data fetching or subscriptions after render, with a dependency array and optional cleanup function.

topics.label: Memoization & Ref Hooks
topics.desc: useMemo and useCallback cache computed values and stable callbacks while useRef holds mutable values across renders, used to tune performance and reach DOM nodes.

topics.label: Context API
topics.desc: React's Provider plus the useContext hook that supply shared values like theme, locale, or current user to a subtree without prop drilling.

topics.label: Custom Hooks
topics.desc: User-defined functions composing built-in hooks to extract and reuse stateful logic across React components, like useDebounce or useFetch, governed by the rules of hooks.

topics.label: Vue
topics.desc: Progressive framework with single-file components, a reactive system, and the Composition API, popular for its gentle learning curve and templates.

topics.label: Svelte
topics.desc: Compiler-first framework that turns components into tiny imperative DOM code at build time, eliminating the virtual DOM for minimal runtime overhead.

topics.label: Angular
topics.desc: Google's batteries-included TypeScript framework with dependency injection, RxJS, and a CLI, favored for large enterprise applications.

topics.label: SolidJS
topics.desc: Reactive framework with JSX and fine-grained signals that updates the DOM directly without a virtual DOM, prized for benchmark-leading performance.

topics.label: Qwik
topics.desc: Resumable framework that serializes app state into HTML and lazy-loads handlers on interaction, targeting near-zero JavaScript on initial load.

topics.label: Web Components
topics.desc: Browser-native custom elements, shadow DOM, and templates offering framework-agnostic encapsulated widgets, used by Lit and design-system libraries.

topics.label: Framework Tradeoffs
topics.desc: Choosing among React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular by weighing ecosystem size, bundle weight, learning curve, hiring, and rendering model.

topics.label: HTMX & Hypermedia
topics.desc: Library that adds AJAX, swaps, and SSE via HTML attributes, reviving server-rendered hypermedia as an alternative to heavy SPA frameworks.

topics.label: Local vs Global State
topics.desc: Deciding what state belongs in a component versus a shared store, the foundational judgment that keeps React and Vue apps maintainable.

topics.label: Prop Drilling
topics.desc: The anti-pattern of threading props through many intermediate components, the problem Context and global stores like Redux exist to relieve.

topics.label: Redux & Redux Toolkit
topics.desc: Predictable centralized store using actions and reducers, with Redux Toolkit cutting boilerplate via slices, Immer, and built-in async thunks.

topics.label: Zustand
topics.desc: Minimal hook-based global store for React with no providers or boilerplate, popular for app state that outgrows useState but not Redux.

topics.label: Jotai & Atomic State
topics.desc: Atomic state libraries like Jotai and Recoil that compose tiny independent atoms, giving fine-grained reactivity and avoiding monolithic stores.

topics.label: Context for State
topics.desc: Using React Context plus useReducer as a lightweight built-in store for low-frequency global values, mindful of its broad re-render cost.

topics.label: Pinia & Vuex
topics.desc: Vue's centralized state stores, with Pinia replacing Vuex to offer a simpler, typed, Composition-API-friendly store for shared application state.

topics.label: Server-State Caching
topics.desc: Libraries like TanStack Query and SWR that fetch, cache, dedupe, and revalidate remote data, separating async server state from local UI state.

topics.label: Client-Side Routing
topics.desc: Mapping URLs to components and switching views via the History API without full page reloads, the navigation backbone of every SPA.

topics.label: React Router
topics.desc: The dominant routing library for React, providing declarative routes, nested layouts, data loaders, and URL params for single-page navigation.

topics.label: Nested & Layout Routes
topics.desc: Composing routes so parent layouts persist while child views swap inside outlets, enabling shared shells in React Router and Vue Router.

topics.label: Dynamic Routes & Params
topics.desc: Path segments and query parameters parsed into typed route data, letting one component render many records like the path users colon id.

topics.label: Route Guards
topics.desc: Navigation hooks that block or redirect unauthorized or invalid transitions, used to gate authenticated pages in Vue Router and React loaders.

topics.label: File-Based Routing
topics.desc: Convention where the filesystem layout defines routes, automating route config in Next.js, SvelteKit, Nuxt, and TanStack Router.

topics.label: Route Code-Splitting
topics.desc: Splitting bundles per route with dynamic import and React.lazy so each page's JavaScript loads on demand, shrinking initial download.

topics.label: CSS Modules
topics.desc: Build-time scoping that hashes class names per file to prevent global collisions, a common styling approach in React and Vue projects.

topics.label: Tailwind CSS
topics.desc: Utility-first framework composing styles from atomic classes in markup, with a JIT compiler purging unused CSS for tiny production bundles.

topics.label: Utility-First CSS
topics.desc: Styling philosophy of composing single-purpose classes directly in markup rather than writing custom rules, popularized by Tailwind.

topics.label: CSS-in-JS
topics.desc: Writing component-scoped styles in JavaScript with libraries like Emotion or styled-components, enabling dynamic, prop-driven theming at runtime.

topics.label: styled-components
topics.desc: A CSS-in-JS library that creates styled React components via tagged template literals, colocating dynamic styles with component logic.

topics.label: Zero-Runtime CSS
topics.desc: CSS-in-JS that extracts styles to static stylesheets at build time, like Vanilla Extract and Linaria, avoiding runtime style injection cost.

topics.label: Design Tokens
topics.desc: Named primitives for color, spacing, and typography stored as variables that keep styling consistent and drive theming across a product.

topics.label: Theming & Dark Mode
topics.desc: Switching design tokens at runtime via CSS custom properties or context to support brand themes and light and dark color schemes.

topics.label: Controlled vs Uncontrolled
topics.desc: Whether React state or the DOM owns an input's value, the central choice shaping how forms are wired and validated.

topics.label: React Hook Form
topics.desc: Performant React form library using uncontrolled refs and subscriptions to minimize re-renders, with built-in validation and resolver adapters.

topics.label: Formik
topics.desc: Earlier React form library managing values, touched, and errors through controlled state, now largely superseded by React Hook Form.

topics.label: Schema Validation
topics.desc: Declaring data shapes once and validating against them with Zod, Yup, or Valibot, sharing rules between forms and API boundaries.

topics.label: Zod
topics.desc: TypeScript-first schema library that validates data and infers static types from the schema, widely used for forms, env, and API parsing.

topics.label: Form UX & Errors
topics.desc: Inline error display, dirty and touched tracking, focus management, and accessible messaging that make validation feel responsive and humane.

topics.label: Submission & Actions
topics.desc: Handling submit with optimistic updates, pending states, and server actions, increasingly via progressive-enhancement APIs in Next.js and Remix.

topics.label: Component Libraries
topics.desc: Prebuilt, styled widget kits like MUI, Ant Design, and Chakra UI that supply buttons, modals, and tables to ship product UI faster.

topics.label: Headless UI Primitives
topics.desc: Unstyled, accessible behavior primitives from Radix UI and Headless UI that hand you logic and ARIA while leaving all styling to you.

topics.label: shadcn/ui
topics.desc: Copy-paste component collection built on Radix and Tailwind that you own in your codebase, blending headless logic with editable styling.

topics.label: Design Systems
topics.desc: A shared library of components, tokens, and usage guidelines that enforces visual and behavioral consistency across an organization's products.

topics.label: Storybook
topics.desc: Workshop for developing and documenting UI components in isolation, enabling visual review, interaction tests, and a living component catalog.

topics.label: Accessible Components
topics.desc: Building widgets with correct ARIA roles, keyboard navigation, and focus management so menus, dialogs, and tabs work for assistive tech.

topics.label: Icons & Assets
topics.desc: Tree-shakable icon sets like Lucide and Heroicons delivered as components, plus SVG sprite strategies for crisp, themeable UI iconography.

topics.label: Client-Side Rendering
topics.desc: Shipping a minimal shell and rendering everything in the browser with JavaScript, the classic SPA model with fast navigation but slow first paint.

topics.label: Server-Side Rendering
topics.desc: Generating HTML on the server per request for fast first paint and SEO, then hydrating it into an interactive app via Next.js or Nuxt.

topics.label: Static & Incremental Generation
topics.desc: Pre-rendering pages to static HTML at build time, optionally regenerating them on demand or on a schedule (ISR), for CDN-fast delivery via Astro and Next.js.

topics.label: Hydration & Islands
topics.desc: Attaching client JavaScript to server-rendered HTML to make it interactive, with islands and partial hydration limiting that costly work to interactive parts.

topics.label: Server Components & Streaming
topics.desc: React components that run only on the server and ship zero JavaScript, streamed in chunks through Suspense boundaries and concurrent rendering in the Next.js App Router.

topics.label: Next.js
topics.desc: The leading React meta-framework offering file-based routing, SSR, SSG, ISR, server components, and server actions for full-stack web apps.

topics.label: Astro
topics.desc: Content-focused meta-framework that ships zero JavaScript by default and uses islands to embed React, Vue, or Svelte components selectively.

topics.label: Remix, Nuxt & SvelteKit
topics.desc: Full-stack meta-frameworks pairing routing and server data with their base framework: Remix and Nuxt and SvelteKit for React, Vue, and Svelte respectively.
